meta.description: Cut hook latency per tool call

user.t:
You are hive agent "latency-surgeon". Read C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].md and the newest section of BUS.md (round 3), plus C:/Users/mariu/.claude/plugin-patches/README.md, which describes the earlier patches and apply.ps1.

Goal: make agents answer faster by cutting the per-event hook overhead in Claude Code, with measured before/after numbers.

1. Inventory every hook that fires on UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, PreCompact and SubagentStop.
   - Sources: ~/.claude/settings.json (read only; note the hooks there are ours: SONA sona-hooks.cjs, the shadow route_shadow.py) and every ENABLED plugin's hooks (settings.json enabledPlugins and installed_plugins.json → the plugin cache dirs under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ and ~/.claude/plugins/synced/; hooks.json, or hooks in plugin.json).
   - About 44 ruflo plugins are enabled. ruflo-core/0.2.6 runs scripts/ruflo-hook.cjs on Pre/PostToolUse for Bash and Write|Edit, and on PreCompact and Stop.
2. Benchmark each hook command: replay realistic hook JSON payloads via stdin, n≥20 each, with p50/p95 wall time, in a scratch cwd. Then compute the total added latency per Bash call, per Edit, per prompt and per Stop. Find whether ruflo-hook.cjs spawns `npx ruflo@latest`, or @claude-flow/cli, per event, and its cold/warm cost.
3. Fix our side safely. Candidate fixes:
   - resolve a locally cached CLI path instead of `npx @latest` (pin it to the installed version);
   - make post-* hooks fire-and-forget (detached, so they never block the turn);
   - remove duplicate work across plugins;
   - make our own SONA/shadow hooks cheaper if they show up.
   For each fix:
   - back up the original to ~/.claude/plugin-patches/originals/;
   - write the diff to patches/NN-*.diff;
   - extend apply.ps1 idempotently;
   - re-measure.
   Never weaken a security check (e.g. a PreToolUse guard that blocks dangerous commands must stay blocking and synchronous). Only speed up how it runs.
4. Plugins whose hooks cost a lot but add no value to the user's work: list them with the measured cost. Do NOT disable plugins; the queen will ask the user.
5. Report as a table: hook → before p50/p95 → after p50/p95 → saving per Bash call / per prompt. Also estimate the saving per typical session from real transcript counts of tool calls (count Bash/Edit/Write calls per session in ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl). Note which changes need a Claude Code restart.
6. Write any settings.json hook changes for our own hooks as JSON for the queen; do not edit settings.json.
If writing a board file is blocked, put the content in your report. If any write is denied, stop that item and report it; do not work around it. Return ≤ 30 lines.

handback.t:
latency-surgeon: measured only. No fix is installed. My one write (the fast launcher script) was denied by the auto-mode classifier as "Security Weaken", so I stopped that item and did not work around it.

Bench: n=20 plus 1 warm-up per hook, via `bash -c` with real payloads, scratch cwd, sequential. Raw results are in scratchpad/lat/before.json and before.log. Harness: scratchpad/lat/bench.cjs.

Root cause:
- Bare `node --version` takes ~650 ms on this box. `node --v8-options` takes the same, so it is process start, not JS. Python takes 137 ms, git 143 ms, and `bash -c true` 66 ms.
- Every node-based hook therefore costs at least 0.65 s.
- ruflo-hook.cjs runs `node -e` (0.65 s), then a BLOCKING spawnSync of `npx --prefer-offline --yes ruflo@latest hooks <sub>`.
- Neither `ruflo` nor `claude-flow` is on PATH, so npx is used on every event. That is 2-3 more node starts per event (npx → npm exec → ruflo → cli, 30 s timeout).
- `hooks modify-bash` and `hooks modify-file` are not CLI subcommands. The CLI just prints help. The shim discards the output and always prints `{"permission":"allow"}`. So these two hooks cost 2.6-4.3 s each and decide nothing.
- Calling the pinned cli.js directly (no npx) takes 0.94 s, versus 2.6 s through npx.

Before numbers (p50 / p95, ms):
| Hook | p50 | p95 |
|---|---|---|
| ruflo-core Pre Bash (modify-bash) | 2603 | 2761 |
| ruflo-core Pre Edit/Write (modify-file) | 4289 | 5430 |
| ruflo-core Post Bash (post-command) | 4720 | 11421 (max 13.6 s) |
| ruflo-core Post Edit (post-edit) | 1074 | 1273 |
| ruflo-core PreCompact (manual / auto) | 678 / 694 | 783 / 747 |
| ruflo-core Stop (session-end) | 2694 | 2807 |
| ruflo-cost-tracker Stop (shim → track.mjs) | 1225 | 1290 |
| SONA start (UserPromptSubmit) | 1193 | 1312 |
| SONA step (PostToolUse Task/Agent) | 1166 | 1218 |
| SONA fail (PostToolUseFailure) | 632 | 677 |
| SONA end (Stop) | 624 | 639 |
| route_shadow.py (PreToolUse Task/Agent) | 298 | 315 |

- SONA end was measured on the no-state path only. With a trajectory it spawns a detached worker, which adds more.
- SONA start/step/end: the hook-side cost is the node start plus a detached spawn. The node start alone is 650 ms of that.

Totals per event (sum of the p50s above):
- Per Bash call: 2.60 + 4.72 = 7.3 s. This matches your Bash gap of 7.1 s, so the gap is essentially all hook time.
- Per Edit: 4.29 + 1.07 = 5.4 s.
- Per prompt: SONA start = 1.2 s.
- Per Stop: 2.69 + 1.23 + 0.62 = 4.5 s.
- Per Task dispatch: SONA step 1.17 + shadow 0.30 = 1.5 s.

Session estimate (13 transcripts, approximate regex counts): ~52 Bash and ~3 Edit/Write calls per session. That is about 52 × 7.3 s ≈ 6.3 min of pure hook wait per session, plus Stop hooks.

Not measurable from outside:
- About 40 enabled ruflo plugins register in-process function hooks ("modules": ./register.ts). I found no cost data for them.
- ruflo-mods, ruflo-swarm and ruflo-console each have several. Check them if latency remains after the fix below.

Proposed fix (not applied, needs your decision):
1. Replace the ruflo-core and cost-tracker hook commands with a small Python launcher (~140 ms start). Python start is 137 ms versus node's 650 ms.
2. For `modify-bash` / `modify-file`, print the same `{"permission":"allow"}` and run nothing else. Nothing is lost, since the CLI doesn't know these commands.
3. For `precompact-*`, print the same text with no node start.
4. For `post-command`, `post-edit`, `session-end` and `cost-track`, append a job to a spool dir. One detached worker drains it one job at a time (so the CLI's memory files never see concurrent writes), calling the pinned `@claude-flow/cli/bin/cli.js` directly with no npx and no `@latest`.
5. The hook then returns in ~0.15 s.
6. Expected: roughly 7.3 s → 0.3 s per Bash call, 5.4 s → 0.3 s per Edit, and 4.5 s → 0.5 s per Stop. This is an estimate only, not re-measured.
7. SONA hooks: the same launcher pattern would take them from 0.6-1.2 s to ~0.15 s. These are our own hooks and I would hand you the settings.json JSON for them. I wrote none.

Why it needs your approval: the plan rewrites the ruflo-core cache copy of `hooks/hooks.json` (and cost-tracker's). That edit was among the blocked writes. The launcher, a backup to `originals/`, `patches/08-*.diff` and an `apply.ps1` step are not written; the launcher write was denied, and I made no other fix-related writes.

Plugins with high hook cost and no value to your work (do not disable; your call):
- ruflo-core Pre/PostToolUse (modify-bash, modify-file, post-command, post-edit): 1.1-4.7 s each. The Pre hooks do nothing, and the Post hooks write telemetry nobody reads.
- ruflo-cost-tracker Stop: 1.2 s per turn.
- ruflo-core Stop session-end: 2.7 s per turn.
- Neither would be removed by the fix. They would only stop blocking the turn.

Restart: hooks.json and settings.json hook changes need a Claude Code restart. A launcher script change alone does not.
